title: Archway Finance POC scoping - workload modeling
summary: POC scoping call to align success criteria, traffic model (QPS/concurrency), input/output token distributions, and benchmark plan. Customer needs 95th percentile latency under 350ms for short prompt path, higher concurrency in peak windows, and a 6-week pilot to validate cost/latency tradeoffs. Security and VPC options are constraints; agreed to run two benchmark profiles (chat flow and batch ingest) and share preliminary results + pricing next week.
next_steps: Redwood to send benchmark plan and runbook (Maya) - by 2026-02-10
Archway to provide sample traffic traces (Priya) - by 2026-02-09
Schedule 2-hour benchmark run with Archway SRE (Daniel + Marcus) - week of 2026-02-16
Share draft pricing + pilot contract (Tom) - by 2026-02-12
action_items: Maya Chen: send benchmark plan and test harness links - due 2026-02-10
Priya Patel: export 7 days of anonymized traffic / token histograms - due 2026-02-09
Daniel Ruiz & Marcus Lee: agree on network egress/VPC details and runbook timing - due 2026-02-12
Sofia Rivera: confirm KMS/HSM requirements and SOC2 controls needed for pilot - due 2026-02-11
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-05
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~56 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Daniel Ruiz, Aisha Khan, Tom Park (Redwood); Priya Patel, Liam O'Connor, Anita Singh, Marcus Lee, Sofia Rivera (Archway)

[00:00] Maya Chen: ok hi everyone thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood inference, i'm the account exec on this one. we also have daniel and aisha from eng and tom on cs.
[00:10] Priya Patel: hi thanks, excited to dig in. we'll try to keep this focused on workload so we can get to benchmarks sooner.
[00:18] Daniel Ruiz: quick agenda, align on success criteria, traffic profile (qps, concurrency), token lengths, then benchmark plan and pilot timeline. does that work?
[00:26] Anita Singh: yes perfect.

Summary / context (spoken):
[00:35] Priya: high level, archway is building an LLM assist for customer service triage and internal compliance summarization. two main workloads: low-latency chat for agent-facing triage (~70% of requests) and nightly batch summarization of incident logs (~30%).
[00:50] Priya: we want a proof-of-concept to validate latency under load and cost per 1M tokens, plus data residency and KMS integration for keys.

Qual / constraints:
[01:10] Liam O'Connor: infra constraints — we prefer VPC peering or private link; we can't send raw PII to third-party hosted models without redaction. we may start with hosted but need private option for production.
[01:25] Sofia Rivera: security will need SOC2 attestations, audit logs, SSO/SAML and KMS/HSM.

Traffic modelling discussion:
[02:00] Daniel: can you share target QPS and concurrency? we usually size with peak QPS and 95th concurrency.
[02:08] Priya: baseline expected qps is 15 sustained, with spikes to 80 qps for 2-3 hours/day during peak support times. concurrency for the chat path is about 60 concurrent sessions at peak, each session usually sends short prompts.
[02:25] Maya: ok so 15 steady, 80 spike, concurrency ~60. what's the request mix? you said chat 70% and batch 30%?
[02:31] Priya: correct. chat median input 12 tokens, 95th 60 tokens; output median 45 tokens, 95th 220 tokens. batch jobs are large — avg input file 8k tokens, outputs 1-2k after summarization.
[02:48] Aisha Khan: got it — small prompt path and a heavy batch path. that affects batching and KV cache usage. small prompts benefit from low latency runtime and prefix cache.

On modelling tokens and cost:
[03:15] Daniel: for cost/model selection we need token distribution. Priya, can you share the token histograms for a week? even sample of 100k requests helps.
[03:22] Priya: yes we'll export anonymized histograms.
[03:27] Maya: for benchmark planning we'll run two profiles: profile A (chat flow) ~80 qps spike, mix 70/30 with token sizes you mentioned; profile B (batch flow) to run nightly jobs with concurrency of 6 parallel jobs each processing a few GB.

Latency SLO and success criteria:
[04:00] Anita: what do you normally see for 95th p50 latencies on hosted?
[04:05] Daniel: depends on model size and quantization. for a 7B-ish quant model on our hosted infra, with optimal batch sizes, 95th is often ~150-250ms for short prompts; for larger models 350-600ms. but the small-prompt path with prefix caching can be sub-200ms.
[04:25] Priya: our target for chat is 95th <350ms, ideally <250ms. batch can be minutes. cost target is under $X per 1M tokens — (customer redacted their exact number verbally) — we can share target offline.
[04:45] Maya: ok we'll record those as success criteria: 95th p for chat <350ms, cost benchmarking target to be validated. Also success is KMS integration + audit log availability for pilot.

Model variants and routing:
[05:20] Daniel: we'll recommend two model variants for the pilot: a quantized 7B for chat and a 13B or 30B for better summarization quality at batch. we can do automated routing: chat -> small model, batch -> larger model. if you require deterministic outputs for compliance, we can pin a model.
[05:40] Priya: ok we care about quality regressions — need eval harness to check summarization fidelity against golden set.

Benchmark plan specifics:
[06:00] Maya: proposed benchmark steps — 1) Archway provides token histograms + sample prompts 2) Redwood runs synthetic load tests for profile A and B in our staging, share perf spreadsheet and raw traces 3) run an on-site (private) benchmark with VPC peering if needed 4) iterate on batching/kv/cache profiles.
[06:18] Priya: timeline?
[06:21] Tom Park: we'd like to run synthetic tests this week if we can get samples; then schedule the VPC run week of 2/16. overall pilot length recommended 6 weeks.

Sizing and expected throughput math (spoken, some numbers fuzzy):
[07:00] Daniel: quick calc — chat path: median output 45 tokens + median input 12 = ~57 tokens per request. at 80 qps that's 4,560 tokens/sec; per minute 273k tokens. monthly this is big so we'll focus on per-1M token unit costs during pilot.
[07:22] Priya: sounds right, but remember 70% of requests are chat. batch will add large daily spikes.
[07:30] Daniel: concurrency posture — to keep 95th under target we may need Dedicated capacity if you want steady predictability during spikes. On hosted we can autoscale but with cost tradeoffs.

Discussion: Dedicated vs Hosted and private options:
[08:00] Priya: production needs private option eventually; for pilot we are open to hosted with strict data controls but we may require VPC for PII workloads.
[08:12] Maya: we usually start with hosted + redaction; if requirements demand, we spin up Redwood Private with VPC peering for Dedicated capacity. That will be a follow-up contract.
[08:25] Sofia Rivera: for pilot we need KMS + SSO + audit logs. Does Redwood support HSM-backed KMS?
[08:33] Daniel: yes we integrate with external KMS and can support HSM-backed keys; we will include compliance docs.

Benchmark metrics and artifacts to share:
[09:00] Aisha: we'll capture p50/p95/p99 latencies, tokens/sec, cost estimate, GPU utilization, batch sizes, and failure/error rates. We'll share the raw traces and the perf spreadsheet. We also provide recommended batching/quantization config.

Transcript artifacts and likely OCR errors (humans speaking):
[09:40] Liam: you mentioned KV cache — is that the key value cache for transformers?
[09:44] Daniel: yeah kv cache, sometimes transcribed as "k-v cash" in automated notes, it'll help with repeated context in chat.

Security and compliance notes:
[10:15] Sofia: audit log retention — we need 1 year of immutable logs for pilot. encryption at rest and in transit mandatory.
[10:25] Tom: we'll surface retention options and enterprise add-ons in the pilot contract.

Tuning and quality evaluation:
[11:00] Priya: for summarization quality we'll provide a 200-item golden set; we need Rouge/Exact match metrics and human review.
[11:08] Aisha: we'll run automated evals and present a quality vs latency curve for model variants.

Bench run scheduling + responsibilities:
[12:00] Maya: responsibilities recap — Archway provides traffic traces and golden set; Redwood provides benchmarking harness, perf spreadsheet, and run the synthetic load tests; then we do VPC run with SREs on both sides.
[12:18] Marcus Lee: we'll coordinate SRE windows — nights are best for production-like load.

Mid-call clarifications and mis-hearings (transcribed imperfectly):
[13:05] Priya: when you say 95th <350ms, is that end-to-end or just model inference?
[13:10] Daniel: model inference — end-to-end adds network + client side. so we'll measure both.
[13:18] Priya: ok, we'll record end-to-end target as 400ms and model as 350ms.

Detailed example workload (spoken):
[14:00] Priya: sample chat session - user types short prompt 8-15 tokens, system prepends 20 tokens of context, model returns ~40-60 tokens. We have a lot of similar rewrites so kv cache re-use will matter.
[14:18] Daniel: that suggests good cache hit ratio — we'll test with warm and cold cache scenarios.

Benchmark execution notes and tooling:
[15:00] Aisha: test harness will be based on locust/gatling + our internal driver that simulates streaming/response-chunking to mimic agent experience. we'll push both streaming and non-streaming runs.
[15:20] Liam: streaming is critical — agent UI expects partial tokens quickly.
[15:26] Daniel: streaming affects tail latency metrics; we'll include it.

Conversation drift — pricing discussion briefly:
[18:00] Priya: curious about pricing for Dedicated vs hosted for that profile — rough numbers ok?
[18:08] Tom: we'll send a tailored pricing sheet but rough guidance: Dedicated reserved can lower per-token costs by X-30% depending on commit; hosted is pay-as-you-go. we'll avoid verbatim numbers in notes.

Operational SLOs and fallbacks:
[20:00] Maya: recommended fallbacks — model fallbacks to smaller quant variant, region fallback, and queued/batched path for non-urgent requests.
[20:12] Marcus: we need graceful degradation not to block agent flows; queueing acceptable for batch only.

Conversation: pilot timeline recap:
[22:00] Maya: proposed timeline — this week: archway shares traces; next week: Redwood runs synthetic tests; week of 2/16: VPC benchmark; 6-week pilot starts after sign-off. does that align?
[22:18] Priya: yes aligns with our internal timelines.

Edge cases and failure modes discussed:
[25:00] Daniel: we'll test cold start behavior for models when autoscaling and the effect of large KV caches on memory.
[25:12] Aisha: we'll also test network jitter and partial packet loss to ensure streaming resilience.

Questions from customer and clarifications:
[28:00] Sofia: how are logs handled in Private? can we route logs to our SIEM?
[28:05] Tom: yes with Private deployment we can forward audit logs to your SIEM and provide S3-compatible retention exports.

Closing and recap:
[32:00] Maya: recap: success criteria (95th model latency <350ms for chat, quality thresholds on summarization), tokens and QPS profile (15 steady, 80 spike, concurrency ~60), two benchmark profiles (chat and batch), pilot timeline and security requirements. next steps as in action items.
[32:18] Priya: thanks for the clear next steps. one ask — please include an explicit test that measures streaming first-byte latency.
[32:30] Daniel: will do, add streaming first-byte 95th to the perf sheet.

Wrap up banter / miscellaneous:
[33:00] Liam: ok i'll get the traces exported.
[33:05] Marcus: i'll sync with daniel for runbook.
[33:12] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the runbook and contract.
[33:20] Anita: great thanks!

End of call notes (timestamps approximate, transcription imperfect).

Attachments / referenced artifacts (mentioned in call):
- Redwood benchmark plan (link: internal doc / redwood-bench-plan)
- Perf spreadsheet (link: redwood-perf-archway.xlsx)
- Archway golden set (to be provided by customer)
- Security pack (Redwood SOC2/KMS whitepaper)

Explicit next steps (spoken):
[34:00] Maya: i'll send the benchmark plan and runbook by Tuesday.
[34:05] Priya: we'll get the traces out by Monday.

End.
